root_cause: PR #13505 optimized INCR/DECR (and related commands) to avoid re-serializing the integer to a string for the reply, by replying directly from the heap-allocated robj ('new') that was just stored into the keyspace, rather than from a stack-local integer copy. However the reply-generation call was left positioned after signalModifiedKey()/notifyKeyspaceEvent(), which can re-enter into module keyspace-notification subscriber callbacks. Those callbacks run with full API access (including RM_StringDMA) to the key that now holds 'new', so they can free/reallocate the buffer 'new' points to before the deferred reply call reads it. Previously, replies used a stack copy of the integer value (or values were small/shared integer objects that aren't actually freed by dict replacement), so no live reference into freed heap memory was retained across the notification call.
findings: incrDecrCommand() was changed (in PR #13505) to reply to the client with addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new) -- reading the string value directly from the 'new' robj that now represents the key's value -- instead of replying with the integer value that had been copied onto the stack (addReplyLongLong(c, value)). This reply call was placed AFTER signalModifiedKey() and notifyKeyspaceEvent() are invoked.
